applyNested(bytes32,bytes32,bytes).details: Contract, caller, value and transition index are taken from the call itself and      hashed into the leaf, so a frame applied by anyone but its signed parent, with any      other value, or out of order fails the leaf check. The parent must also report this      leaf as its pending child, which it does only while executing the `NESTED` op that      names it; without that, a parent that forwards arbitrary calls could be made to      apply the frame outside its tree.

gasKillerProtectedRanges().details: A compile-time constant of this contract's code, validated once by the constructor      (see `constructor`), so it can't be malformed once deployed. Prefixed like no other      SDK getter because a generic `protectedRanges` could already exist in a consumer.

getMessageHash(uint256,bytes4,bytes).details: The digest is scheme-agnostic. Off-chain code can compare this against each digest      format to learn which one a deployed consumer signs.

getMessageHashWithValue(uint256,bytes4,b.details: Named apart from `getMessageHash` because an overload would rename the generated      off-chain binding of the existing function.

inTransition().details: External contracts that read Gas Killer state and can be called mid-transition      (directly or transitively via a `CALL` update) should check this and fail      closed — mid-transition storage is not a quorum-signed state.

returns.count: The total number of tracked state transitions

supportsInterface(bytes4).details: Adds the `IGasKillerNested` extension, which the router probes on every frame      contract of a tree; a root that does not report it settles flat.

verifyAndUpdate(uint32,bytes,uint256,byt.details: `msg.value` is bound into the digest, so the transition settles only with exactly      the value the task was analyzed with: a deposit cannot be credited without its ETH,      and no surplus can be sent. Value moved by `CALL`/`CREATE`/`CREATE2` updates is fixed      inside the signed `storageUpdates` and paid out of this contract's balance, which      includes `msg.value`; a shortfall reverts the whole transition (`RevertingContext` for      a CALL, `DeploymentFailed` for a CREATE/CREATE2).

params.nonSigners: operators that did not sign, strictly ascending.
params.referenceBlockNumber: block at which stake/keys are evaluated by the registry.

verifyAndUpdateBatch((uint32,bytes,uint2.details: Each applied submission is checked exactly as a standalone `verifyAndUpdate`      would check it — same digest, same registry verification — so batching changes      nothing for the off-chain signing path. Transitions apply in order; the      `guardTransition` latch is held across the whole batch, and any failing      sub-transition reverts the entire batch.      A submission whose `transitionIndex` is already settled is SKIPPED (not      validated, not applied) rather than reverting the batch: settlement is      permissionless, so a third party who lifts one submission from the mempool      and settles it standalone could otherwise nullify the whole batch with one      cheap front-run. An index below the counter was either settled or jumped over      by a transition that moved the counter forward, so it can never settle.      Reverts (`InvalidTransitionIndex`) only on a genuine gap — an index above the      next expected one.      Batch assemblers: a `CALL` state update gives its target the gas the trace gave      it, often all that's left (see `StateChangeHandlerLib`). A greedy/griefing target      in an early sub-transition can therefore starve every later one in the same batch,      reverting the whole (atomic) batch — no partial-state hazard, but it does nullify      the amortization this function exists for.      Each submission's digest binds its own `value`, and `msg.value` must cover the sum      over the submissions actually applied (`InsufficientBatchValue` otherwise), so no      applied transition is credited ETH the batch did not bring. The check is "covers"      rather than "equals" because a skipped submission must not revert the batch. The      surplus, such as a front-run item's share, is refunded to `msg.sender` once every      update has applied. A sender that can't accept it leaves it in this contract      rather than reverting the batch.

params.submissions: The transitions to apply, in order of ascending transition index.

verifyAndUpdateTree((bytes32,uint256,byt.details: The registry checks the signature and the signed expiry once and caches the      approval for the rest of the transaction; every callee frame reads that approval      instead of re-verifying. A tree always carries an expiry leaf, so its root can never      equal a single-transition digest and the two settlement paths cannot replay each      other's signatures. The root leaf binds `msg.value` exactly as `verifyAndUpdate`'s      digest does, so the tree settles only with the value it was analyzed with; value      moved by `NESTED` ops comes out of this contract's balance just as a `CALL` op's does.

applyNested(bytes32,bytes32,bytes).notice: Apply this contract's frame of an approved tree.

gasKillerProtectedRanges().notice: The storage ranges a signed program may not change: the SDK's own slots merged         with the consumer's `_protectedRanges()`, in ascending order. Empty when the         consumer has opted out of the check (`_unsafeDisableStorageGuard`); a guarded         contract always lists at least the SDK's two ranges, five behind a proxy.

getMessageHash(uint256,bytes4,bytes).notice: Compute the expected message hash for a transition settled with no ETH

getMessageHashWithValue(uint256,bytes4,b.notice: Compute the expected message hash for a transition settled with `value` wei

inTransition().notice: True while a state transition (or batch of transitions) is being applied

pendingChild().notice: The leaf of the child this contract is calling right now, or zero.

stateTransitionCount().notice: Return the current number of state transitions that have occurred

supportsInterface(bytes4).notice: Query if a contract implements an interface

verifyAndUpdate(uint32,bytes,uint256,byt.notice: Verify an aggregate Schnorr quorum signature and apply the state updates.

verifyAndUpdateBatch((uint32,bytes,uint2.notice: Verify and apply a sequence of independently signed state transitions in         one transaction, amortizing the intrinsic and cold-access costs across the         batch (sub-transitions after the first verify at warm-access prices).

verifyAndUpdateTree((bytes32,uint256,byt.notice: Settle a nested tree whose root frame belongs to this contract.
